about: Canonical per-icon hover motion for the shared glyph set (icons.json). One design per icon, matched to what that icon's action DOES — never one generic tilt for everything. Every surface (browser CSS, desktop Qt, extension) implements THIS table rather than inventing its own; browser/tests/iconMotion.test.js pins it against icons.json and css/animations.css.
units: Lengths and origins are in the 24x24 viewBox user units every glyph is drawn on, so they scale with the rendered icon. Angles are degrees, positive = clockwise on screen (SVG y-down). Durations are milliseconds.

trigger.on: pointer hover of the CONTROL that holds the glyph (button, .btn-icon, .btn-icon-text, .idle-create-btn, .coord-tab, .pill-toggle, .accent-dd-trigger, .accent-dd-opt, .name-edit-btn, .project-menu-item, .ctx-item)
trigger.disabled: INCLUDED. A greyed control still answers the pointer — it shows its tooltip and its disabled reason (browser layout.css keeps pointer-events on it for exactly that) — and the glyph is what the pointer is on. Freezing it made the control read as a dead area rather than as one that cannot act right now: the motion says what it WOULD do, the grey says it cannot yet. Qt: do not gate on isEnabled().
excluded: .is-loading — the busy spinner already owns the glyph's transform
.swapping — a face mid-swap already owns it
[id^="toggle-"] — the fold chevrons: their rotation is STATE (open/closed), not hover feedback
trigger.reducedMotion: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce cancels every motion here — no transition, no keyframes, glyph stays in its rest pose. The rest pose IS the correct end state for all of them (settle ends where it started; hold is pure feedback), so nothing is lost.
trigger.layout: Transform / stroke-dashoffset only. Nothing here may change a box, so no control can reflow.

portingNotes.qt: Drive each part with a QVariantAnimation on the glyph's own 24-unit space and rasterize through the existing iconSet.cpp path; `origin`/`originSelf` map to the QTransform pivot. `hold` runs forward on enter and backward on leave; `settle` runs once, forward, on enter. Two parts sharing a hook animate in markup order, `stagger` ms apart.
portingNotes.qtReducedMotion: REQUIRED: honour support::motionReduced() (STENCIL_NO_ANIM=1) — see trigger.reducedMotion. As of this writing three desktop motion helpers do NOT: ShimmerOverlay, LogoHoverFx and guiHelpers::spinIcon() animate regardless, unlike faceSwap / filterFade / menuReveal / modalReveal. The icon-motion port will sit on those helpers, so fix the check centrally rather than inheriting motion that ignores the preference.
portingNotes.extension: The extension ships a SUBSET of icons.json (its own checked-in copy, pinned by browser-extension/tests/dataParity.test.js) — implement only the designs for the glyphs it carries, from the same CSS shape as browser/css/animations.css.

modes.hold: Transitions to `to` while hovered and eases back on leave. Feedback that persists while the pointer rests.
modes.settle: Plays `keyframes` once on hover, then rests at the base pose. For motions that must return to the default (grow/shrink, typing dots, a spin).

partFields.hook: class on the sub-element(s) inside icons.json this part moves; null = the whole glyph. Several elements may share a hook (see `stagger`).
partFields.origin: [x, y] transform origin in view-box units; omitted = the glyph centre [12, 12].
partFields.originSelf: true = the part transforms about its OWN centre (CSS transform-box: fill-box), not a point in the glyph. For dots/handles that scale in place.
partFields.stagger: ms added per element sharing the hook, in markup order.
partFields.to: hold only — the pose held while hovered.
partFields.keyframes: settle only — [{ at: percent, ...pose }], `at` ascending from 0 to 100.
partFields.dashArray: settle only — stroke-dasharray (view-box units) the part needs for a dashOffset draw-on.
partFields.pose: any of translate [x,y], rotate, scale, scaleX, scaleY, skewX, rotateX (needs `perspective`), dashOffset. Absent = identity.

chevron-up.action: collapse / move up; fold toggles opt OUT (rotation there is state)

pencil.note: the nib makes one short stroke and lifts

check.note: the tick draws itself, the way you'd write it — unhurried (2× the old 320ms, user decision)

x.action: close / clear / disconnect — one motion for all three: they all mean “make this go away”
x.note: the two strokes are drawn one after the other, the way you'd cross something out; each is 12√2 ≈ 16.97 units long. 1.5× the base 180ms draw-on, deliberately slower than the other settle designs

crop.note: the two brackets close in on the region

rotate-ccw.note: one FULL turn the way the button turns the image, so the glyph comes to rest exactly as it started — a partial tilt held on hover only hinted at the turn

rotate-cw.note: the mirror of `rotate-ccw` — same turn, the other way

stop.note: restrained: the block clamps down — a stop has no direction to move in

line.action: line draw mode — the sibling of `rect`; both anchor the same two drag handles, only what joins them changes
line.note: the segment draws itself between the handles, the way a drag would, and the handles pop as it lands

rect.note: the same motion as `line`: the box draws itself between the same two handles

rect-filled.note: it stamps in at once — the point of the action

eraser.note: it actually ERASES: the pad sweeps right along the line under it and that line vanishes from behind the pad, then the pad comes home and the line is written back — the action mimed, not a generic wobble. The baseline runs (22,21)→(7,21), 15 units, so a POSITIVE dash offset eats it from the x=7 end the pad starts on; 4 units of offset track the pad's own 4-unit travel

undo.note: the arrow draws itself slowly, tail to head: the shaft (11 + a r5 half turn + 4 ≈ 30.7 units) is drawn from its far END — a NEGATIVE dash offset, so the ink advances backwards along the path towards the head — and the head is struck last. Direction is still the meaning: undo's head points left, redo's right

redo.note: undo's mirror: the same draw-on, on a glyph pointing the other way

dots.note: the three dots bounce left to right — the typing/pending idiom

trash.note: the lid lifts off the can, hinged at its left end

download.note: the arrow travels DOWN into the tray

upload.note: the same arrow, UP — direction is the whole difference between the pair

copy.note: the two sheets separate, so you see there are two

clipboard.note: the clip lifts, the way you'd open one

paste.note: the arrow drops INTO the board — same direction idiom as download

save.note: the disk slides up into place from below, the way a save writes UP into the project list — the one settle that does NOT overshoot: a disk seating itself never bounces

file-text.note: the two text lines write themselves, top line first

folder.note: the front panel tips open towards you, hinged on the folder's bottom edge

layers.action: projects — the stack of saved work
layers.note: the three layers fly in and assemble into the icon, bottom first

more.note: the dots spread apart — the menu about to open out

moon.note: the crescent WAVES — a small damped rock about the glyph centre, each swing reversing the last and settling upright. Small on purpose: a crescent tipped far enough reads as a different shape

sun.note: the sun TURNS — but by exactly ONE RAY. The glyph has eight of them, 45 degrees apart, so a single ray-space is the smallest turn that still comes to rest looking untouched: the `gear`'s one-tooth idea on a sun. A whole revolution had to be fast to fit a hover and read as a spin rather than a turn. Its twin the moon waves instead — a turn is plain on a rayed disc and plain nonsense on a crescent

maximize.note: the four corner brackets EXTEND outward to enter; on a control already in fullscreen they RETRACT inward instead, so the motion always shows where you are going

minimize.note: the corner brackets draw IN — the way out of fullscreen, the mirror of maximize's

fit.note: the small inner frame GROWS towards the outer one — fitting the image to the window

link.note: the two chain links close together and join

incognito.note: the disguise comes apart: the hat lifts off while the glasses drop away from it

lock.note: the shackle lifts a little, as if about to unlatch

gear.note: the gear turns exactly one tooth (45 degrees), so it comes to rest looking untouched

palette.note: the wells of paint light up in turn

help.note: the question mark gives a quick tremor in place. TRANSLATION, not rotation: turning the mark about the icon centre swings it out of its own ring

info.note: restrained: the “i” bobs for attention — an info mark has no action to mime

refresh.note: half a turn — the glyph is point-symmetric, so it rests looking identical

calendar.note: restrained: the binder rings bob — a date has no motion of its own

image.note: the picture is DRAWN inside its frame — the ridge (≈22.6 units of polyline) draws itself and the little sun DROPS in from just above it, a beat later. Nothing crosses the frame's outline, which sliding the contents in from below did: the sun's top (8.5 − r1.5 − a 1-unit half stroke = 6) clears that outline's inner edge (3 + 1) by 2, so 1.6 is the whole drop there is — it lands with a 0.3 overshoot rather than more height

function.note: the ƒ writes itself: the curve draws top to bottom, then the crossbar strikes through it, the way you'd write an f

message.note: the bubble draws itself, tail to rim, the way you'd sketch one. The typing dots belong to `sparkle`, which is the glyph that HAS dots

eye.note: the pupil glances left, then right

share.note: all three nodes light up in turn, top to bottom — a plain downward sweep across the glyph, the same read as the server icon's LEDs and the layers icon's stack. Lighting only two of the three read as one being broken, so all three play. They SWELL rather than travel: each node sits on the end of a connecting line, and a move big enough to read pulled it off that end. The glyph is drawn top-to-bottom, so markup order IS the sequence.

monitor.note: the screen lifts clear off its stand and settles back — the image being handed to another app. A held 1.2-unit nudge was half a pixel at toolbar size and read as no motion at all, which is the whole reason this table exists

server.note: the status LEDs blink, top unit then bottom

globe.note: the meridian narrows — the globe turning on its axis

refresh-cw.action: live sync to file — the same wheel as `refresh`, turning a WHOLE revolution: a sync runs and completes, so the wheel comes back to where it started instead of resting half-turned

lightbulb.note: the bulb swells as it lights, hinged on its base

alert.note: a short shake — the universal “look at this”

flag.note: the cloth waves on its pole

ruler.note: restrained: the rule slides along its own length, the way you'd lay it down

sparkle.action: the AI assistant — a chat bubble with three dots
sparkle.note: the dots type, left to right

send.note: the plane takes off along its own heading

plus.note: DRAWS itself the way you'd write one — the vertical stroke first, then the horizontal struck through it as the first lands (markup order IS the sequence); each stroke is 14 units

minus.note: SHRINKS, then settles back — a minus that swelled read as “increase”, which is the bug this table exists to prevent

plus-circle.action: new editor / new connection / blank page
plus-circle.note: the cross inside draws itself — the vertical stroke, then the horizontal, 8 units each; the ring stays put

swap.note: the two arrows slide past each other, each the way it points

compare.action: turn on the split compare view
compare.note: the frame draws itself first (a rounded 18x18 square, rx=2: 4 straight 14-unit sides + a full circle's worth of corner ≈ 68.5 units), then the divider draws top to bottom through it, the way you'd rule a split AFTER the page is there to split

mic.action: voice input — talk instead of typing
mic.note: the mic itself PULSES once — from its resting size up to large and back — about the glyph centre, as if it just picked up a voice, while the sound waves GROW out of it, smallest first: each of the three arcs per side starts tiny against the capsule and swells to its resting size in turn, inner → middle → outer, the way sound spreads. Left and right mirror. (At rest the arcs are hidden while the mic is off and shown while it listens — that visibility is the control's state, styled outside the motion sheet; the hover reveals them for the swell either way)

description.action: the project's description — a sheet of text
description.note: the sheet's three text lines WRITE themselves, top to bottom, one after another (dash draw-on, 8 / 8 / 5 units), the way a description is typed

keywords.action: the project's keywords — a bullet list
keywords.note: the three bullet rows (• —) APPEAR one after another, top to bottom: each slides in from the left, small, and settles at its place

file-down.action: download the layout FILE to disk
file-down.note: the arrow inside the page travels DOWN, as the tray pair's does

file-up.action: upload a layout FILE from disk
file-up.note: the same arrow, UP — direction is the whole difference between the pair

script.note: the cog in the page's corner turns one tooth, like the settings gear

draw-mode-icon.action: line / rectangle draw mode — the browser's own inline pair (svgArt.json `drawMode`, served as DRAW_MODE_ICON by ui/icons.js), which is the canonical `line`/`rect` pair on a 16-grid instead of 24. A surface drawing the canon uses those two designs; this entry is only for the inline faces.
draw-mode-icon.note: the canonical `line`/`rect` design at 16 units: the shape DRAWS ITSELF between the two drag handles the way a drag would — the segment (10√2 ≈ 14.2) or the box it spans (4×8 straights + a r1 corner each ≈ 38.3) — and the handles pop as it lands. The face swap owns everything else about this button

swap-click-turn.trigger: CLICK, not hover — the one motion in this table that answers a press
swap-click-turn.note: the swap glyph turns one full revolution CLOCKWISE as the orientation it toggles flips, so the press is acknowledged by the thing that changed. Reuses `icmTurnCw` and rotate-cw's timing: one spin feel across the app.
